correctness.rationale: Every clique of C_{3r}^r is classified as lying in one consecutive r+1-window or one of r equilateral triangles. The window subcomplex collapses by explicit free-face pairs and by the cited girth theorem to C_{3r}; its H_1 carries the reflection sign. The r oriented relative triangle generators map integrally by the all-ones surjection onto H_1 of this circle, giving integral H_2=kernel(sum) with all higher and lower reduced homology zero. The dihedral action on relative generators is the signed permutation action, so its integral kernel has the stated character. Independent finite structure, augmented boundary-rank, and signed Lefschetz checks replay; finite computations are not used as infinite proofs. The r=1 boundary and even/odd reflection cases are included.

originality.rationale: Corollary 6.7 in arXiv:1104.0433 supplies the nonequivariant wedge multiplicity; this is not claimed as new. Proposition 7.2 in arXiv:1410.4336 supplies dihedral characters for circular-arc NERVE complexes, whereas its Section 8 map from a cyclic clique complex is nonequivariant with respect to the full natural D_{3r} action: the target has different cyclic indexing and the map does not commute with rotation at wraparound. Consequently the established two statements do not imply the exact D_{3r} action on the clique complex. The present proof identifies the signed integral lattice for all r directly. Full primary-text mathematical comparisons, an exact-source search, mathematical-result database searches and earlier claims found no stronger covering statement; bibliographic uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The first one-third critical scale is a natural transition in cyclic Vietoris--Rips topology, and the known wedge-of-spheres rank does not determine the action of its geometric dihedral symmetries. The result identifies the full integral lattice for every size, a reflection-parity distinction and the rational homology of the full quotient. These are motivated intrinsic topological invariants and go beyond reproducing a known table or routine specialization. The limited scope and absence of integral quotient and higher-critical-scale results are explicitly stated.
